doc.title: Jane Bunnett interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 25, 2024

chapter: Women in jazz and being Canadian
title: Being Canadian on the New York scene; Paul Bley's advice
summary: She says being Canadian works against her in New York, recalling Paul Bley telling her to drop it from her bio; Paul Shaffer joke.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: be Canadian, because I’m out of — I know you’re looking at me funny there. But yeah, because I’m not on the — that’s sort of changing a tiny bit now too but you know New York is very centric to hey we don’t know about you — yeah. We don’t know about you. I’m not on the New York scene. I’m in Toronto. I’m based here. I’m Canadian. I remember Paul Bley telling me to take it out of my bio, take it out, take the Canadian out. Bless Uncle Paul we call him — take it out. You know? I remember him telling me to get an American address. Just get a box number in New York City, it’s so much better than saying you’re Canadian.
Well Paul Shaffer didn’t take it out.
Paul Shaffer. I say hey man, Paul Shaffer’s Canadian.
